## Walkthrough Azure network interface service code is refactored to classify backend address pools for load balancers using name-suffix matching (`"-v6"` suffix) instead of index-driven and PrivateIPAddressVersion approaches. Nil-guards are added for backend address pools, and NAT rule iteration is conditioned on `nicSpec.NatRule` being non-nil. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Backend Pool Classification Logic**
`pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces.go`, `pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces_stack.go`|Refactored pool selection from index/length-gated iteration to suffix-based classification. Backend pools are now grouped into IPv6 vs non-IPv6 by checking if `BackendAddressPool.Name` ends with `"-v6"`, with nil-guards added. NAT rule iteration decoupled and conditioned on `nicSpec.NatRule` presence.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~20 minutes

**Actionable comments posted: 1** > [!CAUTION] > Some comments are outside the diff and can’t be posted inline due to platform limitations. > > > >
> ⚠️ Outside diff range comments (2)
> >
> pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces.go (1)
> > `212-227`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_ > > **Attach the selected NAT rule once, to its owning IP family.** > > Line 213 uses the frontend list as a multiplier but always appends the same `nicSpec.NatRule` entry. On a dual-stack LB, that can put the same NAT rule ID into both `loadBalancerInboundNatRules` and `loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6`, even though an inbound NAT rule belongs to a single frontend IP configuration. This block also needs nil/bounds checks before dereferencing `lb.FrontendIPConfigurations` and indexing `lb.InboundNatRules`. > >
> 🤖 Prompt for AI Agents > > ``` > Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. > > In `@pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces.go` around lines > 212 - 227, The code currently loops frontend IP configs but always appends the > same inbound NAT rule index, causing the same rule to end up in both > loadBalancerInboundNatRules and loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6; instead, locate > the inbound NAT rule entry once (using (*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule]), > nil-check lb.FrontendIPConfigurations and lb.InboundNatRules and bounds-check > *nicSpec.NatRule, then inspect that inbound rule's FrontendIPConfiguration (or > compare its referenced frontend ID to entries in *lb.FrontendIPConfigurations) > to determine whether it is IPv4 or IPv6 and append a single > network.InboundNatRule{ID: ...} to only loadBalancerInboundNatRules or > loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6; finally keep the existing assignments to > nicConfig.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules and > nicConfigV6.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules but only after these checks and the > single appended rule. > ``` > >
> >
>
> pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces_stack.go (1)
> > `167-177`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_ > > **Don't fan out one NAT rule across every frontend.** > > Line 168 appends the same `nicSpec.NatRule` once per frontend config, so a dual-stack LB produces duplicate references while `loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6` still stays empty. The direct index on `(*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule]` can also panic when the slice is nil or shorter than the requested rule. > > >
> Proposed fix > > ```diff > - if nicSpec.NatRule != nil { > - for range *lb.FrontendIPConfigurations { > - loadBalancerInboundNatRules = append(loadBalancerInboundNatRules, > - network.InboundNatRule{ID: (*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule].ID}) > - } > - } > + if nicSpec.NatRule != nil { > + if lb.InboundNatRules == nil || *nicSpec.NatRule < 0 || *nicSpec.NatRule >= int64(len(*lb.InboundNatRules)) { > + return fmt.Errorf("load balancer %s does not have inbound NAT rule %d", nicSpec.PublicLoadBalancerName, *nicSpec.NatRule) > + } > + rule := (*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule] > + loadBalancerInboundNatRules = append(loadBalancerInboundNatRules, network.InboundNatRule{ID: rule.ID}) > + // Append to loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6 only after resolving the selected rule's frontend family. > + } > ``` >
> >
> 🤖 Prompt for AI Agents > > ``` > Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. > > In `@pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces_stack.go` around > lines 167 - 177, The code is appending the same NAT rule once per frontend which > duplicates references and leaves the IPv6 list empty, and it directly indexes > (*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule] which can panic if the slice is nil or > too short; change the logic in the block that handles nicSpec.NatRule so you (1) > only append the referenced NAT rule once (do not loop over > lb.FrontendIPConfigurations to append the same rule), (2) guard access to > lb.InboundNatRules by checking it is non-nil and that *nicSpec.NatRule < > len(*lb.InboundNatRules) before dereferencing, and (3) decide whether to push > the rule into loadBalancerInboundNatRules or loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6 by > inspecting the corresponding frontend IP configuration’s IP version (iterate > frontends to find the matching frontend IP config for that NAT rule or otherwise > determine v4/v6) and then set nicConfig.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules and > nicConfigV6.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules appropriately. > ``` > >
> >
> >
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces_stack.go`: - Around line 151-165: The current classification in networkinterfaces_stack.go that builds backendAddressPoolsV6 by checking strings.HasSuffix(*pool.Name, "-v6") fails because the load balancer creators (publicloadbalancers_stack.go and internalloadbalancers_stack.go) do not emit names with a "-v6" suffix; either (A) modify those creators to also create/emit IPv6 backend pools with the "-v6" suffix for the same base pool names (so networkinterfaces_stack.go will find them and attach nicConfigV6), or (B) change the classification in networkinterfaces_stack.go to detect IPv6 pools by inspecting pool metadata (e.g., examine pool.BackendAddresses or pool.BackendIPConfigurations for IPv6 addresses or an explicit IPFamily tag) instead of relying on the name suffix; update the logic that populates backendAddressPoolsV6 and backendAddressPools and ensure nicConfigV6 is appended to any pool identified as IPv6. --- Outside diff comments: In `@pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces_stack.go`: - Around line 167-177: The code is appending the same NAT rule once per frontend which duplicates references and leaves the IPv6 list empty, and it directly indexes (*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule] which can panic if the slice is nil or too short; change the logic in the block that handles nicSpec.NatRule so you (1) only append the referenced NAT rule once (do not loop over lb.FrontendIPConfigurations to append the same rule), (2) guard access to lb.InboundNatRules by checking it is non-nil and that *nicSpec.NatRule < len(*lb.InboundNatRules) before dereferencing, and (3) decide whether to push the rule into loadBalancerInboundNatRules or loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6 by inspecting the corresponding frontend IP configuration’s IP version (iterate frontends to find the matching frontend IP config for that NAT rule or otherwise determine v4/v6) and then set nicConfig.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules and nicConfigV6.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules appropriately. In `@pkg/cloud/azure/services/networkinterfaces/networkinterfaces.go`: - Around line 212-227: The code currently loops frontend IP configs but always appends the same inbound NAT rule index, causing the same rule to end up in both loadBalancerInboundNatRules and loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6; instead, locate the inbound NAT rule entry once (using (*lb.InboundNatRules)[*nicSpec.NatRule]), nil-check lb.FrontendIPConfigurations and lb.InboundNatRules and bounds-check *nicSpec.NatRule, then inspect that inbound rule's FrontendIPConfiguration (or compare its referenced frontend ID to entries in *lb.FrontendIPConfigurations) to determine whether it is IPv4 or IPv6 and append a single network.InboundNatRule{ID: ...} to only loadBalancerInboundNatRules or loadBalancerInboundNatRulesV6; finally keep the existing assignments to nicConfig.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules and nicConfigV6.LoadBalancerInboundNatRules but only after these checks and the single appended rule. ```
